name: 1626 Prairie Avenue — brick house with a frame front bay, the north half of the pair with 1628, K01 frontage assembly

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 33.774, v -4.226 m from the middle of the rear lot line): the rear wall and the south (party) wall are laid on 1628's (T-2355's house_1628_prairie, whose rear wall stands at u 33.774 and north wall at v -4.226 in this lot's frame), so the pair closes on one party wall, 0.21 m south of the 1904 parcel line and inside the trace's 2.46 m fit; the traced main part's own rear wall is at u 33.6-33.8 and its south edge at v -4.03. Through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check, so its own fit residual, 3.08 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed. Rotation -0.579 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.
placement.symbolic_location: 1626 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1626 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).

footprint.note: The main body, the three-storey block the sheet draws across the whole front of the lot: 12.25 m deep (the traced main part's front block runs u 33.6-46.15; the draft's fit, with front_body_from_u_m 33.5, takes u 33.75-46.0) and 8.0 m along the front, from 1628's north wall to v 3.774, 0.24 m inside the lot's north line where the trace's north edge runs (v 3.75-4.00). The fit stops at v 3.0 only because the trace takes the sheet's '12 12 8' numerals, printed against the north wall at u 39.7-40.3, for a 0.9 m bite out of the house; the raster shows an unbroken wall there. The draft's own main rectangle (u 19.75-46.0 by 3.5 m, the rear range and the house in one strip) is not a house a K01 body can be. The rear pieces behind the south part of the rear wall (u 19.6-33.75: the 1B piece and the 2B wing with its frame end) wait for T-2347, which teaches K01 a traced rear wing.

stories.note: '3B; rear 1B/2B' printed on the 1911 sheet: three full storeys over a basement, the same as 1628's. The rear 1B and 2B are the pieces behind the house, which wait for T-2347.

construction.note: The register reads the map's colours as 'brick'. T-2356: built as a brick house, front and all — K01's `brick` construction (T-2341), the K03 common brick on every wall, with stone dressings on the street front; the frame bay is the sheet's yellow, built in timber.

principal_floor_m.note: 1628's raised principal floor over the basement the sheet's 'B' prints: a pair built together keeps one floor line. Inside the K01 contract's principal_floor range [0.8, 1.8]; it solves to whole risers.

storey_heights_m.note: Floor to floor, diminishing upward, 1628's own three, so the pair's floors, sills and cornice run level across the party wall. No source reads this house's heights.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: A 13-inch brick wall, inside the contract's masonry range [0.23, 0.45], as 1628's; the sheet prints no wall thickness for this lot.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: Common brick, a 13-inch wall, as the front.

service_wall_brick.note: The sheet colours the house brick; the fabric, bond, heads, string course and grime are the K03 library's common buff brick in common bond (the one panel k03_brick lays), on all four walls, as 1628's. No photograph of 1626 has been read, so the brick's colour and bond are the kit's, not the house's.

street_front_trim.note: The street front's window heads as 1628's, so the pair reads as one build: the K09 stone lintel under a cornice hood on the two lower storeys and K01's flat stone lintel on the low third; the door keeps K01's flat stone lintel. Only the door and the third storey show them here, the frame bay standing in front of the rest. No source shows 1626's heads.

wall_head.note: A K10 bracketed timber cornice (data/components/prairie_1904/k10_cornices.json) round all four walls, as on 1628, its partner, and 1608, 1612 and 1616 up the row. No source reads its eave. No cresting: none is read.

roof_form.note: A hip roof, the one K01 builds (k01.roof.hip), low-pitched behind the bracketed eave, as 1628's and as the draft drew it. No source reads this roof; a three-storey pair of this period may as well have stood under flat roofs behind a cornice, which K01 cannot build yet (T-2350 asks for K05's flat roof).

roof_pitch_deg.note: Low, inside the contract's ordinary range [25, 45]: an Italianate hip over a full third storey, with no attic to light. 30 because, on this 12.25 x 8.0 m plan, it is a pitch the K05 roof union this kit dresses its caps on parts cleanly (see docs/RESEARCH/k01-1626-frame-bay-2356). Tinned rather than slated, because K04's Pennsylvania slate is cut for a 45 degree roof.

eave_overhang_m.note: A deep Italianate eave over the brackets, as 1628's; the fascia and soffit close it. 0.6 m is an eave the K05 union builds at this roof's pitch (see roof_pitch_deg).

stair_landing_depth_m.note: A landing one door-swing deep before the threshold.

stoop_width_m.note: The stoop half again the door's width.

entrance_bay.note: The door at the north end of the 8.0 m front, so the pair's doors stand at their outer ends, 1628's at the south (the draft rules' row frontage-20-007); the frame bay takes the south part of the front, where the sheet draws it.

front_bays.note: Three bays across the 8.0 m front, south to north: two behind the frame bay, whose own windows light the two lower storeys there, so they are windows on the third storey only; and on the north the door with a window a storey over it.

side_bays.note: None: the south wall is the party wall with 1628 and is blank, standing on 1628's own blank north wall.

rear_bays.note: Three windows a storey in the 8.0 m rear wall, north to south. The sheet's 1B piece joins the south part of this wall (v -4.0 to about 0.6): when T-2347 stands it, the window at 6.6 m becomes the opening into it.

sash_by_storey.note: Double-hung sash, diminishing upward, inside the contract's sash ranges, 1628's own, so the pair's windows match.

basement_lights.note: Area lights in the front wall, the basement the sheet's 'B' records; on this front the frame bay and the stoop stand where they would go, so none is cut.

roof_covering.note: Painted tin in standing seams, K04's cover for a roof too low for its slate, with copper ridge and hip rolls and copper flashings, as 1628's. No source reads 1626's roof.

chimneys.note: Two brick stacks on the ridge over spine walls between the front, middle and back rooms, as 1628's and 1608's, 1612's and 1616's; the draft drew two. No source reads this house's chimneys.

rainwater.note: K04's half-round copper gutter round the eave and round copper downpipes to splash stones: one at the front's north corner beyond the stoop (the frame bay holds the south part of the front), two at the rear corners. None on the south wall, the party wall, and K01 stands none on its north wall. All reconstructed.

window_kit.note: Every window from the K06 kit: two-over-two double-hung sash, the kit's commonest form, not a reading of this house; the basement lights the kit's area light.

entrance_kit.note: The K07 kit's four-panel door under a two-light transom at the head of a straight stone stoop solved from the principal floor. front_yard_m is the street grid's own distance: the front stands 9.37 m behind the Prairie Avenue street line (lot street_u 55.397 less the front at u 46.024) and the walk begins 1 ft further out (row_66 margin band), 9.68 m.

north_bays.note: Three windows a storey along the north wall, front to rear, one to each room of a three-room-deep house, as 1628 has on its south: the wall faces the side yard toward 1620 (whose house stands 7.9 m off it), so it is windowed like a free side, which K01 builds on a record naming north_bays (T-2342).

bays.note: The sheet's two-storey frame bay on the Prairie face (T-1840 census s20-1626-f: '2-storey frame (yellow) bay'), so its PLACE, its two storeys and its timber are inferred from the map; its form is the kit's. The trace draws the yellow piece about 2.0 m out across the south 4.7 m of the front (s20fp-1626-b1 p1 and p2, s 0.3-5.0 m from the party wall); built as the kit's canted bay, 3.7 m at the wall, 1.1 m out, centred 2.75 m from the party wall, so its eaves clear the K10 cornice's corner bracket. Built in K01's `frame` fabric (T-2356): a painted timber body, the dark green of the kit's painted joinery, over a brick plinth, with painted timber bands, sills and heads, two storeys under a low tin hip. The storeys, windows, paint and roof are reconstructed (liberty L-k01-1626-brick-frame-bay-2356). The sheet draws the same yellow piece on across the party line in front of 1628's north half, under one dashed street side; it may be one two-tier frame piece across the pair's centre rather than 1626's bay alone. That reading is left open: 1628 is built without it (T-2355).

boundary.note: T-3216: no picture of this front is held, so the boundary is a STATED RECONSTRUCTION on the west side of the block's pictured fronts, every one of which closes its street line and gates its walk: 1612's photograph (an iron spear fence on its curb, a pair of entrance gates at the stoop's foot and a gate across the south passage), 1620's 1874 engraving and 1898 sketch (an iron lattice on its base with gate piers at the walk), 1616's boarded street line in the same 1874 plate, and 1638's photograph (iron bars on a stone base between gate piers). Built as the K11 kit's spear fence on its curb, the plainest of them and the block's photographed iron, with the kit's pair of entrance leaves on stone piers, 1.3 m clear on the stoop's centre, standing open (drawn 70 degrees) as 1612's photograph and both pictures of 1620 show their entrance gates. No side gate: the house stands 0.00 m from its south lot line, less than the kit's gate needs between a pier and the wall (0.9 m clear past a 0.5 m pier), so there is no passage to gate and the iron runs unbroken from the lot line to the entrance (K11's T-3216 rule). The street line is parcel prairie_1626's street corners (data/street_grid/1904.json) carried into this frame, 9.365 m before the front. The lot's sides are the same parcel's, s 0.21 and 8.24; the south one is put on the house's south wall, s 0.0, because the parcel's line as fitted falls 0.21 m inside the wall, well within the sheet's 3.08 m fit residual. RECONSTRUCTED: the fence's kind, height and line, its gates and their set; liberty L-k11-fences-1600-block-3216.

yard.note: T-3216 (the owner, 2026-10-27: every worked house's walk to its door, its gates and its boundaries to their pictures; where no picture shows them, a stated reconstruction consistent with the block). No picture of 1626's front is held. The walk is laid on the block's pictured fronts (1612's photograph shows a light paved walk from the public walk through its open entrance gateway to the stoop's foot, and 1616's and 1621's walks are built on it): flags from the stoop's foot through the entrance gate, the gate's width, to the inner edge of the public walk; the lawn covers the rest of the front yard inside the iron. RECONSTRUCTED: the walk's line, flags, width and wear, the lawn and its bare strip are the K14 kit's (data/components/prairie_1904/k14_condition.json) aged from the phase's own year, as the kit's rule is; no service walk is built (no picture shows a side passage's floor); liberty L-k14-walks-1600-block-3216.

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B brick dwelling (D), the north half of a pair attached to 1628; 2-storey frame (yellow) bay on the Prairie face' (T-1840 census s20-1626-f). Carried to 1904 on the T-1840 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 20.
what_it_supplies: The Illinois Central / Michigan Central right-of-way and, from the 16th Street row south about 60 m, the water's edge beside it, as of 1911
Footprints, lot lines, street widths (66 ft; 16th Street 50 ft), addresses, material by colour and story counts for Indiana Av. to the tracks, 16th to 18th Street, as of 1911
Its own printed Scale of Feet, which the georeference uses as its scale
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: T-2356 (piece 2 of T-1862) refines the district draft (T-2334) in place under the same id: the main body is rebuilt from the K01 frontage assembly and its kits — K03 brick on all four walls, K06 sash, K07 door and stoop, K09 window heads, K10 bracketed cornice, a K04/K05 hip — and the sheet's two-storey frame bay on the Prairie face is a K08 canted bay in K01's new `frame` fabric (painted timber over a brick plinth), as T-2355 built its partner 1628. What is read: the 1911 Sanborn sheet 20 (storeys '3B', brick, the north half of a pair attached to 1628, the traced main body, the yellow two-storey bay) through the T-1840 census. Its SOUTH wall is the party wall it shares with 1628 and is built blank, standing on 1628's north wall; its north wall, over the side yard toward 1620, is windowed. Everything else is reconstructed and recorded as L-k01-1626-brick-frame-bay-2356. The sheet's rear pieces — a 1B brick piece, then a 2B brick wing ending in a one-storey frame piece, behind the south part of the rear wall — wait for T-2347 (K01's traced rear wing). No photograph, plate or description of 1626 has been read; a later reading that finds one replaces the kit's choices here.
called: 1626 Prairie Avenue — brick house with a frame front bay, the north half of the pair with 1628
